notes: Group E audit (live-tile, mainframe, mesh-gradient, micrographics, mid-century). Line refs are js/aesthetics/<key>.js and css/aesthetics/<key>.css. Schema gaps: (1) usedBy.where takes one range, so moves that span a js hook and a css rule list the main range and name the other in `variant`. (2) The schema has no field for 'colour solver' primitives; contrast-floor-print is recorded as a needs-code move with params so M1 can decide whether the framework ships it as a built-in solver. (3) Most of each style's ~35-component UI-kit CSS (live-tile css 274-711, mainframe 236-610, mesh-gradient 438-750, micrographics 397-727, mid-century 326-737) is a mechanical restyle of the same few material moves; moveCoverage assumes the generator can derive that kit CSS from the moves, which is untested. (4) Fixed non-brand inks (fixed-signal-inks) are board/website only: mid-century's own app block (css 326-331) drops them and uses the brand palette.

styles.name: Live Tile
styles.coreTrick: A true-black or white ground carries hierarchy in huge light lowercase type, while colour lives only on flat zero-radius rectangular tiles on a 4-column 8px-gap grid.
styles.colourRecipe: Ground is fixed pure black (dark) or white (light). The client primary, secondary and accent are each nudged toward black or white until they hold 3:1 on the ground and a white or near-black label holds 4.5:1 on them; a neutral tile is the ink eased toward the ground to 3:1. A muted primary is simply pushed until it reads, so it still works; only one accent tile is allowed per view.

remainder.what: Two-sided colour search: nudge a colour toward black or white by the shortest step that satisfies BOTH 3:1 on the ground and 4.5:1 for its label
remainder.whyCode: Iterative search with two simultaneous constraints and a choice of direction; not expressible as a variable or formula.

remainder.what: Tile wall composition: seven fixed tiles (role, size, count, flip delay, back face), the brand initial on tile one, one accent tile, five sliding squares
remainder.whyCode: Bespoke hand-composed layout table with copy slots and a flip schedule; board art only.

remainder.what: Board list rows turned into tiles by nth-child cycling (3n+1 primary double-wide, 3n+2 secondary, rest neutral) with row internals re-gridded
remainder.whyCode: Re-lays existing list markup positionally; depends on the board's row DOM, not a reusable recipe.

remainder.what: Cards and panels dissolved into the ground; swatches become plain tiles; radius zeroed with a radio-button exemption
remainder.whyCode: Selector-specific overrides of base board parts with exceptions (radio, phone chrome); needs per-selector knowledge.

styles.notes: Most of the look is a short list of rules (ground, radius 0, shadow none, 2px edge, ink-fill selected, light lowercase type). The tile wall and the flip/slide motion are board-only and bespoke. Hover colour is a 14% ink mix kept only while the label reads (js 152-154), a small colour guard.

styles.name: Mainframe
styles.coreTrick: Depth comes from stacking three greys (canvas, layer 1 at 4% ink, layer 2 at 8%) on an 8px grid instead of shadows, with filled fields over a bottom rule, left-aligned 48px buttons and Plex Sans plus Mono type.
styles.colourRecipe: Ground is a near-white with a trace of the brand hue (dark: a cool blue-grey black with 15% brand hue). The client primary is re-derived in HSL until white text on it holds 4.6:1 and it holds 4.6:1 on layer 2 (dark: lifted instead). The secondary button is filled with the ink; the secondary colour only tints the tag pills. A muted primary is pulled darker or lighter in lightness only, keeping its hue.

remainder.what: Primary printing by HSL loop: clamp saturation 30-88, step lightness until 4.6:1 against white (light) or layer 2 (dark)
remainder.whyCode: Iterative colour search against two backgrounds; needs a solver, not a variable.

remainder.what: Muted ink searched until it holds 4.6:1 on canvas and both layers
remainder.whyCode: Multi-surface contrast loop.

remainder.what: Stripe raster with constrained seeded randomness: retry up to 60 times until at least 5 distinct widths and 4 distinct pitches, all multiples of 4; brand initial cut by the stripes through a clipPath over a ghost raster
remainder.whyCode: Seeded generator with rejection sampling and a composed SVG; the constraint set is bespoke.

remainder.what: Hero readout composition: hanging numbered mono rows, perforation hole row, caption, all in one SVG
remainder.whyCode: Hand-placed SVG layout with copy slots.

remainder.what: Board list built as a table with a header row (panels.list) and its responsive collapse
remainder.whyCode: Replaces board markup with a different structure; custom DOM.

remainder.what: IBM Plex Sans 300 @font-face reusing the bundled variable file
remainder.whyCode: Font-asset wiring tied to a specific bundled file.

styles.notes: The layer-stacking and 8px grid are the genuine portable ideas; both reduce to tokens plus a few selectors. Dark mode has its own hue and mix amounts (js 150-163), covered by params on tinted-neutral-canvas and tonal-ramp. Radius 0 has one deliberate exception (tags are full pills, css 100).

styles.name: Mesh Gradient
styles.coreTrick: A clipped band behind the hero is painted with four blended radial lights of the brand colours plus 140 fine sine-wave striations and film grain, while everything below it is opaque white cards with neutral layered navy shadows and the same gradient reused on the primary action, bars and avatars.
styles.colourRecipe: Primary, secondary and accent are pushed 8-10 points more saturated (never darkened) for the band and striations. The client primary prints as the pill fill; a second stop is the primary turned 28 degrees round the wheel, lightness-adjusted until the button label still holds 4.5:1. Canvas stays near white (cards are pure white paper); a muted brand is saturation-boosted so the lights stay luminous, and ink text stays dark ink, never white on the mesh.

remainder.what: Hero art: a product-fragment trio (project card with sparkline, type-spec code tile using the brand's real font names, approval chip) built from live board data and straddling the band's diagonal cut
remainder.whyCode: Reads board rows and chosen fonts, builds real HTML mock UI; bespoke composition.

remainder.what: Hue-turn search: rotate the primary 28 degrees and step lightness until the label holds 4.5:1; syntax-colour lift loop on the dark code tile (6:1)
remainder.whyCode: Iterative contrast solving on rotated colours.

remainder.what: Diagonal sheared band: clip-path polygon cut tied to a container-query-sized cut variable, sitting behind the header and off the right edge
remainder.whyCode: Layout geometry that depends on the board's hero DOM and a bleed variable.

remainder.what: Panels overrides: 01 card gains a spec detail list, 03 list gains a header, stretched card heights, spec-sheet state rows
remainder.whyCode: Replaces and extends board markup per section.

remainder.what: Blended-with-Liquid-Glass rules for app surfaces and the title glow in product screens
remainder.whyCode: Cross-style interaction and per-screen placement; not reusable as a move.

styles.notes: The band, striations and grain are board-only art. The portable parts are gradient-action-carry (kit), layered shadows, pill CTA and the type tracking. The app glow behind the title (css 334-343) conflicts with the app-has-no-art rule and was not made a move. There is also a legacy 'mesh-gradient--classic' block (css 408-437) that was ignored.

styles.name: Micrographics
styles.coreTrick: One giant brand glyph with an offset hairline duplicate is ringed by 8px mono microtype, crop marks, ruler ticks, orthogonal callout leaders and a few canvas-backed sticker panels, so the 80:1 scale contrast is the whole look.
styles.colourRecipe: Printed as one ink on the canvas: the client primary appears only as a few 3-5px marks and the single filled action; secondary and accent get tiny swatch squares. Hazard tape and the caution triangle use a fixed safety colour (orange on light, yellow on dark), never a brand colour. A muted primary barely changes the look because colour is almost absent.

remainder.what: Spec plate composition: glyph measured on a canvas for true ink edges, callout leaders and labels placed from those edges, stickers laid over it (spec table, QR block, hazard tape), a stacked fallback plate for phones
remainder.whyCode: Measures text in a canvas at render time and derives positions; bespoke.

remainder.what: Seeded QR-like block with three finder squares and a seeded body, and seeded barcode bar widths
remainder.whyCode: Procedural generators (kept as the barcode-serial move; the QR block is not in the seed set).

remainder.what: Brand data piped into decoration: hex codes, font names, role rows and per-section data strings
remainder.whyCode: Needs the live palette and fonts; partly tokens but the string templates are bespoke.

remainder.what: Vertical running spec line and four corner crop marks drawn as one pseudo-element each with many stacked gradients
remainder.whyCode: Very long hand-written gradient stacks; a generator could emit them, but the layout is fixed to this board.

remainder.what: Counter-driven chip indexes and section codes ('C-01', 'T.01', 'P.03/04')
remainder.whyCode: CSS counters plus string content tied to board class names.

styles.notes: The identity is concentrated in the hero plate, which is almost all remainder; the kit side is cleanly describable (hairline boxes, crop marks, mono caps, underline fields, ink-filled selection). Round-6 notes in the file header say the plate was rebuilt, so the art evolved a lot while the CSS stayed stable.

styles.name: Mid-Century
styles.coreTrick: A cut-paper poster (jittered-edge sunburst, sun, atom, starburst seal, kidney, sputnik, boomerang) on cream, with the UI as cream cards in 2px walnut outlines with one cut corner and a dotted colour-block header band, pill buttons and fill-bar stats.
styles.colourRecipe: Cream paper, walnut ink and five fixed period inks (mustard, teal, tomato, olive, aqua) are the board's base. The client primary prints as the poster's sunburst, the script word and the main button after being warmed 6 degrees toward yellow with 15% less chroma and its lightness shifted until a cream or walnut label reaches 4.8:1; the secondary and accent get the same warming. In the app, the fixed inks are dropped and the brand palette is used. A muted primary just becomes a muted sunburst and button.

remainder.what: Hero poster: composed layout of sunburst, sun, atom with three coloured electrons, seal with initial, kidney, boomerang and sparkles, seeded by brand name
remainder.whyCode: Hand-placed illustration; the shape primitives are generators (kept in cut-paper-shape-set) but the composition is bespoke.

remainder.what: Jittered-edge outline resampler (mcCut) that makes every shape look scissor-cut
remainder.whyCode: Geometric procedure on path points; could be a generator but needs a point-level shape engine.

remainder.what: Palette swatches turned into five distinct shapes (circle, half-round, leaf, sparkle) per role
remainder.whyCode: Per-role bespoke shape CSS.

remainder.what: Decorative sparkle / starburst SVG data-URIs generated into CSS variables and used as list dots, status marks, rule ornaments and the button starburst
remainder.whyCode: SVG generation inside tokens() feeding CSS url() values; needs code.

remainder.what: Kit restyle in cut paper (calendar, wheel pickers, accordion, carousel, lightbox, pie menus, knob)
remainder.whyCode: Component-specific drawing for 20-odd kit parts; largely derivable from the card, pill and dotted-wall moves but never proven so.

styles.notes: The poster is board/website art only and is mostly remainder. The kit and cards are the portable part. Two fully different looks: board uses fixed period inks, app uses brand colours (css 326-331), so appSafe for fixed-signal-inks is false.
